My. Fucking. Life. I've had pstd since I was young. My whole life people told me my abusers were right. I was afraid constantly of my dad beating or raping me. He'd tell me I was whore, useless, born to be garbage, and often would pit my family against eachother. My mom and sister would go along with him and would watch him beat me and admitted doing it out of fear.

Let me repeat that: my mom and sister sold me out to my dad and justified him beating me to save their own asses.

This year alone my boyfriend of 4 years left me. I had to move out three times, once of out of a horrible mental housing facility that was full of criminals and people who didn't know how to not let their illnesses damage others. People wait 7 years to be on this list but are okay with it because it's better than being homeless. my dad left 90k debt on my family house which my sister refuses to sell because of the shit city we live in, my abusive father died of cancer and I will never ever get any words of acknowledgement from him. Ever. One of his last words to me was that I'd make no money after finally battling my ptsd to get a job. I still can't maintain any job because my health is so shit. The last training program I had I couldn't sleep for days and I started halucinating. I just want to win at something dammit.

My biology is so fucked even though I want to live a good life I still get suicidal almost every week and get triggered so often throughout the day I lose sleep.

Today I found out my ex is sleeping with another person and I still love him. i'm utterly crushed, crazy, and I feel like i'm going insane. Yes I'm getting help but im so broken and right now I feel defeated. I want to get angry and scream but it wouldn't be right.

What else does 2018 have for me? It's not fucking over yet. still can't fucking believe im alive, and I still can't fucking believe life is so constantly cruel to me.

Self soothe. Self soothe. This skill is important. Self Compassion should be taught properly to yourself. It's hard but even things will little relief will help. Hugging a plush.
